title: Structured human interaction contracts
description:
Purpose: Let host applications attach stable action identity, typed resource references, freshness preconditions, expiry, and structured response schemas to Tactus human interactions without coupling the runtime to any host product.

Exclusions:
- Host authorization and persistence.
- External notification delivery.
- Product-specific resource routing.

Definition of Done:
- Existing Human primitives accept and preserve the optional generic metadata.
- Structured review responses are validated deterministically.
- Replay and callback behavior remain compatible.
- Outside-in specifications and quality gates pass.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Started the structured HITL contract increment on a clean feature worktree from develop. The runtime will remain host-neutral: it transports optional action metadata and validates structured responses, while authorization, persistence, routing, and external delivery stay with the host application.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Final local validation is green: 4,203 tests, 449 behavior scenarios, 24 stdlib tests, repository-wide Black and Ruff, and 153 focused structured-HITL/runtime tests. Sandbox acceptance exercised a persisted review and replay successfully. Plexus consumption must wait for these changes to receive a new released Tactus version.
